Sales Director

Success requires securing major DSO framework contracts across the UK and Northern European markets while building a scalable sales organisation capable of supporting rapid regional expansion.

Requirements of the Role
- Proven track record in grid technology sales and partnerships, preferably in LV monitoring, smart grid devices, or related digitalisation technologies for DSOs.

- Deep knowledge of UK and European DSO procurement models (Ofgem, RIIO-ED2 context, ENA standards) and familiarity with Northern European and broader EU utility regulatory frameworks.

- Strong experience in tender preparation, negotiation, and contract award processes.
- Capability to recruit, mentor, and manage sales and pre-sales teams across multiple countries and geographies.

1. Revenue Growth & Market Leadership
- Deliver UK and Northern European revenue growth to €45m within the next three years.

- Drive overall company order book conversion rates, ensuring delivery against Board revenue targets.

2. Strategic Account & DSO Management
- Build and lead relationships with senior procurement, innovation, and operations teams at DSOs across the UK and Northern Europe.
- Secure a minimum of eight long-term framework agreements/contracts across the UK, Northern Europe, and the wider European market with DSOs and white-label partners.
- Position Analog Devices as a trusted partner in LV monitoring and grid digitalisation across the region.

3. Sales Organisation & Leadership
- Structure and lead a high-performing sales team across the UK and Northern Europe.
- Establish KPIs, commission frameworks, and reporting cadence.
- Mentor pre-sales and business development staff to improve win rates and deal velocity.

- Ensure alignment of technical solutions with DSO specifications and regional regulatory incentives.
- Lead business development and execution of white-label partnerships and ecosystem relationships.
- Lead final contract negotiations and framework onboarding.

- Track regulatory changes across the UK, Northern Europe, and wider EU markets and adjust go-to-market strategies accordingly.
- Feed market insights into product roadmap development (e.g., PQ, fault location, digital substations, and grid digitalisation initiatives).
- Shape Analog Devices' market presence at key industry events across the UK and Europe, including ENA, CIRED, Eurelectric, and relevant Northern European utility forums.

Month 2: Early Engagement & Positioning

- Regional bid calendar.

- Regional sales team plan.
- Board-approved growth strategy.

- Minimum five major DSO framework contracts secured across the UK and Northern European markets.
- Fully functioning regional sales organisation with clear reporting and accountability.
- Analog Devices recognised as a leading supplier of LV monitoring solutions across the UK and Europe within three years.

Front-End Fab Category Manager

Shape the Future of Semiconductor Manufacturing at ADI
Analog Devices (ADI) is seeking an experienced Front-End Fab Category Manager to lead sourcing strategies for the critical equipment, services, and supplier partnerships that enable our global wafer fabrication operations. Supporting ADI fabs across Oregon, Washington, Massachusetts, and Ireland, this role sits at the intersection of semiconductor manufacturing, engineering, and supply chain strategy.

This is a highly visible opportunity for a sourcing professional who understands front-end semiconductor manufacturing and has direct experience working with wafer fab equipment, major OEM suppliers, and the technical stakeholders responsible for maintaining world-class manufacturing performance.

The successful candidate will bring deep knowledge of semiconductor front-end tools and supplier markets, along with a proven ability to develop category strategies, negotiate complex commercial agreements, and build long-term supplier partnerships that improve availability, cost competitiveness, and operational resilience.

About the Role
As the Front-End Fab Category Manager, you will own sourcing strategies for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, related services, aftermarket support, spare parts, and supplier partnerships that directly impact ADI's factory performance and future capacity plans.
You will work closely with engineering, maintenance, facilities, operations, and global procurement teams while serving as the primary commercial leader for key fab equipment categories and supplier relationships.

This role requires a combination of strategic sourcing expertise, semiconductor manufacturing knowledge, and supplier management experience to ensure ADI maintains competitive advantage through its equipment and service supply base.

What You'll Do
- Develop and execute sourcing and category strategies for front-end semiconductor manufacturing equipment, services, spares, maintenance support, and related supplier ecosystems.
- Lead commercial relationships with major semiconductor equipment OEMs and service providers.
- Partner with equipment engineering, process engineering, manufacturing, maintenance, facilities, and operations teams to understand technical requirements and align sourcing strategies with fab objectives.
- Drive supplier selection, RFx activities, contract negotiations, and long-term commercial agreements for capital equipment and recurring service spend.
- Negotiate pricing, lead times, service levels, warranty terms, uptime commitments, inventory strategies, and capacity agreements.
- Identify opportunities to improve total cost of ownership, equipment lifecycle management, operational reliability, and supplier performance.
- Develop risk mitigation strategies for critical suppliers, constrained technologies, sole-source dependencies, and long-lead-time equipment categories.

- 5+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier management, semiconductor manufacturing, equipment engineering, or related disciplines.
- Experience developing and executing sourcing strategies within semiconductor manufacturing environments.
- Demonstrated success leading complex negotiations and managing high-value supplier relationships.
- Strong analytical, commercial, and project management skills.
- Ability to influence stakeholders across technical, operational, and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications
- Direct experience supporting semiconductor front-end wafer fabrication operations.
- Strong understanding of semiconductor process equipment used in lithography, deposition, etch, CMP, metrology, inspection, diffusion, implant, wet clean, and related front-end manufacturing processes.
- Experience working directly with major semiconductor equipment OEMs and service suppliers.

- Ability to translate technical requirements into sourcing and commercial strategies.
- Strong executive presence and influencing skills.
- Proven ability to build trusted partnerships with engineering, operations, and supplier leaders.

- Passion for solving complex supply chain and manufacturing challenges.
